acceptance_criteria.criterion: Trusted issuer edge is deployed/reachable at a stable HTTPS URL.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Operational Railway reachability is validated after merge/deploy; this candidate changes the Railway-compatible OpenCode isolation selection only.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: GitHub Actions secret `HUNTER_ISSUE_AGENT_WEBHOOK_URL` is configured to `<issuer-base>/issue-agent/authorize`.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The webhook URL is operator-managed and this candidate neither reads nor commits it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Required issuer verification/runtime configuration is present without committing secrets.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The provider adapter detects Railway's trusted runtime marker and invokes the repository-owned permission sandbox module with the existing Python interpreter; the shim strips publication and authority credentials and applies deny-by-default permissions without committing secrets.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Exact authorized test event passes GitHub trigger -> issuer authorization -> canonical Smart Prompt build/handoff boundary.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The deployed end-to-end event is an operational validation after this candidate is merged. Exact-head hosted validation covers this code candidate.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Missing/invalid authorization or endpoint configuration still fails closed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Explicit sandbox overrides must resolve to an executable or fail; non-Railway runtimes still require bwrap; the Railway shim rejects malformed argv, unexpected binds, invalid roots, and non-OpenCode commands.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No autonomous merge/deploy side effect occurs from the validation event.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The model process receives no GitHub publication credential or governance signing authority; commit, push, rollback, merge, and deploy remain in trusted parent control.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Issue #437 can then be re-authorized through the canonical governed trigger.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Issue #437 is re-authorized only after #441's deployed end-to-end validation succeeds.

findings.evidence: Railway cannot create bubblewrap namespaces. The provider adapter now selects the repository-owned permission sandbox module automatically when Railway's runtime marker is present, avoiding the unavailable kernel namespace operation.

The previous Codex P1 is resolved without prohibited connector paths: no scripts/ or root configuration change remains in the final diff. Selection lives in the allowed src/ provider adapter and is covered by focused tests.
Explicit operator sandbox overrides still win and must resolve; Railway auto-selection does not weaken non-Railway bwrap behavior or silently accept a missing explicit executable.

The application-level permission sandbox is intentionally weaker than an OS namespace boundary; final deployed #441 validation must confirm the pinned OpenCode runtime honors the permission contract before #437 is re-authorized.
